question.problem: Given the curve $r(t)=2t\,i+({t}^{2}-1)\,j$, find all of the points at which ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $r(t)$ are perpendicular.
question.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-1)\,j \\  & =2i+2t\,j\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors $r(t)$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are perpendicular for some value of the parameter $t$ if and only if $r(t)\cdot {r}^{′}(t)=0.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t)\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =0 \\ [2t\,i+({t}^{2}-1)\,j]\cdot (2i+2t\,j) & =0 \\ 2t\cdot 2+({t}^{2}-1)\cdot 2t & =0 \\ 2t(2+{t}^{2}-1) & =0 \\ 2t({t}^{2}+1) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the only solution is $t=0$ since ${t}^{2}+1>0$ for any $t.$

Finally, since

$$
\begin{aligned}r(0)=2(0)\,i+((0)^{2}-1)\,j=-j,\end{aligned}
$$

 we conclude that $r(t)$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are perpendicular at the point $(0,-1).$
